newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, December gains on delivery.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, December gains on delivery.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby December higher on a tight supply of deliverable wheat that has not been spoken for, traders said.
"There is concern over a shortage of deliverable stocks and funds are short the December," a trader said.
As of Wednesday there were 3,682,652 million bushels of wheat registered in Toledo for potential delivery and 20,202 bushels in Chicago.
But "there's only 1.5 million bushels that are uncommitted," the trader said.
There was little fresh input overnight or Tuesday.
The focus was on the spreads with the December/March closing at 13-1/2 cents per bushel, premium December compared with 9-1/2 cents premium December at Monday's close.
"The spreads are on fire and are going to stay that way, maybe until July," he said.

There was little input to skew the market one way or another with news Turkey may import wheat from Argentina a possible bearish scenario. There have been hopes that Turkey soon would buy wheat from the United States.
Wheat closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 4-1/2 cents lower, with December up 3-3/4 at $3.97-3/4.

Wheat futures traders again were reminded of a satisfactory crop coming on for the 1997 harvest with USDA Monday pegging the young U.S. winter crop at 74 percent good to excellent, up from 73 percent good to excellent a week ago and well above the 52 percent good to excellent rating at the same time a year ago.
Rallies in the wheat pit also were thwarted by spillover pressure from Monday's slide which was tied to news Egypt bought 600,000 tonnes of wheat over the weekend, none of it from U.S. stocks.

But technicians this week were starting to cite evidence of mild bullish flags in key moving averages (MA). The four day MA for December closed at $3.96-1/2, 18-day at $3.84-1/4 and 40-day at $4.03-3/8.
The daily nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 58.5 points. The market considers an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market and 70 or more as overbought.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, below the 14,271 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,000 contracts, below the 3,555 traded Monday.
